text:
marta: Heads-up — saw a customer report where a resumed streaming session got double-billed after a client reconnect. sketch of events below, wonder if we're missing an invariant.

rui: Ugh. Can you paste the trace? which router did it hit?

marta: TL;DR: client opens stream -> partial tokens generated -> client times out (client-side) -> reconnects with same session_id but new connection -> server resumes from last ack offset but also replays a small suffix -> billing shows both fragments charged.

marta: Example trace (simplified):
```
IN: conn1 start session S1 -> model emits tokens [A B C D E] (charged 5)
client acked up to C, then network drop
RECONNECT: conn2 start session S1 resume_offset=3 -> runtime replays tokens [D E] to rebuild KV -> model continues from F...
Ledger: showed charge for initial 5 + replay 2 = 7
```

kevin: Was the replayed [D E] actually returned to the client, or only used internally to warm KV cache?

marta: It was streamed to the client (small dup). The client deduped/display logic handled it fine, but billing shows them as distinct output charges.

zara: We currently attribute charges per emitted token per connection. Replay events are not special-cased. That seems like an accounting bug if replay tokens are not logically new tokens.

rui: Two quick options: 1) mark replayed tokens as provisional and avoid finalizing ledger until session end+dedupe pass, or 2) use a dedupe key (session + prefix-hash + sequence) and ignore tokens with same dedupe id. Both have tradeoffs.

kevin: 1) Provisional credits are messy with dedupe windows and customers will see odd provisional balances. 2) Dedup by (session_id, absolute_position) seems clean if we can guarantee absolute_position monotonicity across restarts.

zara: Absolute_position only exists if the client gives us a resume_offset or we persist per-session counters. Some customers don't send resume_offset (they rely on stateless reconnect). For those we'd need a server-side session anchor (sticky) which we don't always have for hosted API.

marta: Real-world tether: the client didn't reliably send resume_offset — it tried to reuse session_id and we did best-effort resume by comparing last tokens in cache. That heuristic caused us to stream duplicates.

rui: If we can't rely on client resume_offset, maybe we should change runtime to perform internal-only replays (no streaming to client) to warm KV, and then resume actual emission only for new tokens. That would avoid billing duplicates entirely.

kevin: Internal-only replay depends on being able to simulate same generation state without sending tokens. For some models we can restore KV and not emit; for others (non-deterministic sampling) we may have to re-sample which would diverge.

zara: Also need to consider tool-calls. If a tool-call happened during the initial run and the replay re-executes tool-call side-effects, that's unsafe. We must not re-run side-effectful tool calls during resume.

marta: Good catch — the customer had a short tool-call (webhook) mid-stream. Our current replay re-invoked the toolcall which caused duplicate external requests and inflated billing + side-effects.

rui: So constraints summary: avoid double billing, avoid re-running tool side-effects, minimize provisional bookkeeping UX noise, and support stateless clients.

kevin: Proposal: implement resume protocol change + server safeguards:
  - require resume_offset OR generate server-side final_position token at commit points (every 512 tokens) that client can use.
  - when reconnecting without resume_offset, runtime does internal-only state rebuild (no tool re-execs) by restoring KV up to last committed checkpoint and then streams only subsequent tokens.
  - for non-checkpointed models, fall back to provisional credit + admin reconciliation.

zara: UX notes: Console should surface provisional credits and exact reason (replay vs toolcall duplicate) and allow auto-refund if duplication rate > threshold. Add telemetry tags: resume_missing, replay_streamed, toolcall_replayed.

marta: Implementable plan for next week: rui/kevin to prototype server-only replay and checkpoint marker. zara to spec telemetry + console change. I'll run a small repro with the customer.

rui: I'll also add a ledger flag "replay_suppressed" so the billing pipeline can ignore tokens with that flag in the same session window.

kevin: One more: add a defensive test in integration harness that simulates reconnects with/without resume_offset and ensures billing delta <= 1 token for expected corner cases.

zara: :thumbsup: and add a note to rollout doc: any resume behavior change must be feature-flagged and opt-in for Dedicated customers.

replay-bot: deploy/ci triggered \nbuild: inference-replay-suppression/branch

marta: Thanks team. I'll paste repro once I have it. We should also review docs so customers know to send resume_offset when possible. :thinking:
